info.description:
# Sprint 09 – End-to-End API Integration Testing

## Sprint Goal

The goal of this sprint is to verify the complete booking lifecycle by executing an end-to-end integration workflow across multiple Restful Booker API endpoints.

This sprint focuses on validating API integration, authentication, request chaining, data consistency, CRUD operations, resource lifecycle management, workflow continuity, response validation, error handling, and ensuring that each API endpoint functions correctly as part of a complete business process.

---

# Collection Workflow

## Plain Text

``` text
GET    /ping
        ↓
POST   /auth
        ↓
POST   /booking
        ↓
GET    /booking/{{bookingid}}
        ↓
PUT    /booking/{{bookingid}}
        ↓
PATCH  /booking/{{bookingid}}
        ↓
DELETE /booking/{{bookingid}}
        ↓
GET    /booking/{{bookingid}}

 ```

---

# Learning Objectives

During this sprint I learned:

- End-to-End API Testing
    
- API Integration Testing
    
- Complete CRUD Workflow Validation
    
- Authentication Testing
    
- Authorization Validation
    
- Resource Lifecycle Validation
    
- Data Consistency Validation
    
- Collection Variables
    
- Request Chaining
    
- REST API Status Code Validation
    
- Positive API Testing
    
- Negative API Testing
    
- Advanced JavaScript Assertions
    
- Collection Runner Execution
    
- Automated Test Validation
    
- Recording Test Execution Results
    
- API Response Validation
    
- Bug Reporting
    
- Using Git for Version Control
    

---

# Collection Scope

## APIs Covered

``` text
GET    /ping
POST   /auth
POST   /booking
GET    /booking/{id}
PUT    /booking/{id}
PATCH  /booking/{id}
DELETE /booking/{id}
GET    /booking/{id}

 ```

---

# Workflow Validation

The collection validates the complete booking lifecycle by verifying:

- API availability
    
- Authentication
    
- Booking creation
    
- Booking retrieval
    
- Complete booking update (PUT)
    
- Partial booking update (PATCH)
    
- Booking deletion
    
- Verification that the deleted booking no longer exists
    
- Request chaining using Collection Variables
    
- End-to-End workflow execution using Collection Runner
    

---

# Test Scenarios

- ✅ Verify complete booking lifecycle
    
- ✅ Verify authentication before protected operations
    
- ✅ Verify deleted booking cannot be retrieved
    
- ✅ Verify workflow data consistency
    
- ✅ Verify repeated workflow execution
    
- ✅ Verify CRUD operation sequence
    
- ✅ Verify request chaining using Collection Variables
    
- ✅ Verify end-to-end workflow execution

---

# Sprint Outcome

The complete Postman collection was successfully executed using **Collection Runner**, validating the entire booking lifecycle from authentication through resource deletion. All requests completed successfully in the correct sequence without manual intervention.

The workflow confirmed successful authentication, booking creation, retrieval, full update, partial update, deletion, and verification that the deleted resource returned **HTTP 404 Not Found**. Request chaining was implemented using Collection Variables, enabling seamless data sharing between requests throughout the workflow.

A total of **8 requests** and **48 automated assertions** were executed with a **100% pass rate**. No unexpected API behavior, server-side errors, or functional defects were observed during execution.

---

# Notes

Sprint 09 represents the successful completion of the **Restful Booker API Testing Project** by integrating every previously tested endpoint into a single automated end-to-end workflow.

Unlike previous sprints, which validated individual endpoints independently, this sprint demonstrates how multiple REST API endpoints interact as part of a complete business process. The workflow verifies API availability, authenticates the user, creates a booking, retrieves the created resource, performs both full and partial updates, deletes the booking, and confirms successful deletion by validating the expected **HTTP 404 Not Found** response.

Special emphasis was placed on API integration, authentication, request chaining using Collection Variables, CRUD workflow validation, data consistency, automated JavaScript assertions, response validation, resource lifecycle management, Collection Runner execution, and professional documentation.

Successful completion of Sprint 09 demonstrates the ability to design, execute, automate, validate, and document a complete API integration workflow following industry-standard QA and API testing practices using Postman.

# Request 01 – Health Check

## Purpose

Verify that the Restful Booker API is online and responding before executing the end-to-end workflow.

This request acts as a prerequisite for all subsequent requests in the collection.

---

# Request Configuration

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Request Name | Health Check |
| Method | GET |
| Endpoint | `/ping` |
| Authentication | None |
| Headers | None |
| Request Body | None |

---

# Full URL

``` text
{{baseUrl}}/ping

 ```

---

# Expected Response

## Status Code

``` text
201 Created

 ```

## Response Body

``` text
Created

 ```

## Response Time

``` text
Less than 5000 ms

 ```

---

# Validation Objectives

- Verify the API is reachable.
    
- Verify the endpoint returns HTTP 201.
    
- Verify the response body equals "Created".
    
- Verify the response time is acceptable.
    
- Verify no unexpected server errors occur.
    

---

# Postman Tests

Validate:

- Status Code = 201
    
- Response Time < 5000 ms
    
- Response Body = "Created"
    

---

# Expected Result

The Health Check endpoint responds successfully, confirming that the API is available and ready for execution of the remaining end-to-end workflow.

# Request 02 – Authentication

## Purpose

Generate a valid authentication token that will be used to authorize all protected requests during the end-to-end workflow.

The authentication token is stored as a Postman collection variable and reused by subsequent requests requiring authorization.

---

# Request Configuration

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Request Name | Authentication |
| Method | POST |
| Endpoint | `/auth` |
| Authentication | None |
| Headers | Content-Type: application/json |
| Request Body | JSON |

---

``` text
{{baseUrl}}/auth

 ```

---

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Content-Type | application/json |

---

# Request Body

``` json
{
    "username": "{{username}}",
    "password": "{{password}}"
}

 ```

---

# Expected Response

## Status Code

``` text
200 OK

 ```

## Response Body

``` json
{
    "token": "abc123..."
}
 ```

- Verify authentication succeeds.
    
- Verify HTTP status code is 200.
    
- Verify the response contains a token.
    
- Verify the token is not empty.
    
- Store the token in the collection variable `token`.
    
- Verify response time is acceptable.

- Status Code = 200
    
- Response Time < 5000 ms
    
- Response contains token
    
- Token is not empty
    
- Save token to collection variables
    

---

# Expected Result

A valid authentication token is returned by the API and stored for use in all subsequent authenticated requests within the workflow.

# Request 03 – Create Booking

## Purpose

Create a new booking using valid booking details and verify that the booking is successfully created.

The generated **booking ID** is stored as a Postman collection variable and used throughout the remaining end-to-end workflow.

---

# Request Configuration

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Request Name | Create Booking |
| Method | POST |
| Endpoint | `/booking` |
| Authentication | None |
| Headers | Content-Type: application/json |
| Request Body | JSON |

---

# Full URL

``` text
{{baseUrl}}/booking

 ```

---

# Headers

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Content-Type | application/json |

---

# Request Body

``` json
{
    "firstname": "{{firstname}}",
    "lastname": "{{lastname}}",
    "totalprice": {{totalprice}},
    "depositpaid": {{depositpaid}},
    "bookingdates": {
        "checkin": "{{checkin}}",
        "checkout": "{{checkout}}"
    },
    "additionalneeds": "{{additionalneeds}}"
}

 ```

---

# Expected Response

## Status Code

``` text
200 OK

 ```

## Response Body

``` json
{
    "bookingid": 1234,
    "booking": {
        "firstname": "John",
        "lastname": "Smith",
        "totalprice": 150,
        "depositpaid": true,
        "bookingdates": {
            "checkin": "2026-08-01",
            "checkout": "2026-08-05"
        },
        "additionalneeds": "Breakfast"
    }
}

 ```

---

# Response Time

``` text
Less than 5000 ms

 ```

---

# Validation Objectives

- Verify booking creation succeeds.
    
- Verify HTTP status code is 200.
    
- Verify response contains a booking ID.
    
- Verify booking ID is valid.
    
- Verify booking data matches the submitted request.
    
- Store the booking ID in the collection variable `bookingid`.
    
- Verify response time is acceptable.
    

---

# Postman Tests

Validate:

- Status Code = 200
    
- Response Time < 5000 ms
    
- Response contains bookingid
    
- Booking ID is valid
    
- Booking data matches request
    
- Save bookingid to collection variables
    

---

# Expected Result

A new booking is successfully created, and the generated booking ID is stored for use in subsequent requests during the end-to-end workflow.

# Request 08 – Verify Booking Deleted

## Purpose

Verify that the booking deleted in the previous request is no longer accessible by attempting to retrieve it using its booking ID.

This request confirms the successful completion of the resource lifecycle and validates that the API correctly returns a **404 Not Found** response for a deleted resource.

---

# Request Configuration

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Request Name | Verify Booking Deleted |
| Method | GET |
| Endpoint | `/booking/{{bookingid}}` |
| Authentication | None |
| Headers | None |
| Request Body | None |

---

# Full URL

``` text
{{baseUrl}}/booking/{{bookingid}}

 ```

---

# Expected Response

## Status Code

``` text
404 Not Found

 ```

## Response Body

``` text
Not Found

 ```

---

# Response Time

``` text
Less than 5000 ms

 ```

---

# Validation Objectives

- Verify the deleted booking cannot be retrieved.
    
- Verify HTTP status code is 404.
    
- Verify the API correctly reports that the resource no longer exists.
    
- Verify response time is acceptable.
    

---

# Postman Tests

Validate:

- Status Code = 404
    
- Response Time < 5000 ms
    
- Resource no longer exists
    

---

# Expected Result

The API returns **404 Not Found**, confirming that the booking has been permanently deleted and is no longer accessible.
